hook_text: Taxi fares: 17, 29, 41, 53. Someone says the rule is times 17. The second passenger proves them wrong.
clip_script: Soweto taxi. One passenger pays R17. Two pay R29. Three pay R41. Four pay R53. Someone says times 17, because 1 times 17 is 17. Check row two: 2 times 17 is 34, not 29. Wrong. Read the steps instead: 12, 12, 12. So times 12. One passenger: 12, but the fare is 17, so plus 5. The bag fee. Rule: times 12 then plus 5. Test every row: 24 plus 5 is 29, 36 plus 5 is 41, 48 plus 5 is 53. All true. Now backwards: a fare of 65. Undo the last step first, like shoes before socks. Minus 5 is 60, divided by 12 is 5 passengers. Same rule in words, in a flow diagram, in the table, in the sentence 12 times box plus 5. A rule must fit every row, not just the first.
visual_style: Whiteboard fare table filling row by row; a wrong times 17 crossed out at row two; a flow diagram walked backwards with shoes and socks icons.
mood: Gotcha moment, then a clean method.
pacing: The false rule exposed, the steps read, the fix found, every row tested, then backwards.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the rule for your own taxi or bus fare at home.
